deck_summary.title: Full-Duplex Voice Agent on a Raspberry Pi

bullets: One clock: the assistant machine's monotonic clock; every stage timestamped (VAD end → ASR final → LLM 1st token → TTS 1st audio → speaker)
E2E = speaker − VAD end; barge-in = stop − speech start
10 phrases × 3 runs; mean + p95; JSON log per run: stage_latency.json (per turn: trials/<id>/stages.jsonl)

run_card.device: Raspberry Pi 5 Model B Rev 1.1 · 8 GB
run_card.cooling: official Raspberry Pi 5 case (built-in fan) · peak 52 °C · throttled never
run_card.network: cloud: Wi-Fi · benchmark link: Wi-Fi, 6 ms round trip

models.ASR: gpt-live-1 (speech to speech: hears and speaks itself)
models.LLM: gpt-live-1 (speech to speech: hears and speaks itself); router gpt-6-luna for look-ups
models.TTS: gpt-live-1 (speech to speech: hears and speaks itself)

models.ASR: gpt-live-1 (speech to speech: hears and speaks itself)
models.LLM: gpt-live-1 (speech to speech: hears and speaks itself); router gpt-6-luna for look-ups
models.TTS: gpt-live-1 (speech to speech: hears and speaks itself)

checks.text: scoring extras: ASR (faster-whisper), pitch/intensity (praat-parselmouth) · not installed: UTMOSv2 quality
checks.fix: pip install -r requirements-score.txt (laptop) to score transcripts and voice change
use Ethernet if you can; Wi-Fi jitter widens latencies
python tools/fetch_datasets.py --force gets the full set

checks.text: rig: direct feed on ws://127.0.0.1:8791 (no audio devices used)
assistant runs on another machine (Pi); fdbench will listen on all interfaces
Pi CPU, memory, temperature and throttling: sent by the launcher during the run (checked when she connects; see the run log)
judge: none (timing and turn-taking metrics only; judge later with `score`)
